fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. She opens that basket, sees a crying little boy, and says, “This is one of the Hebrew children.” (Exodus 2:6) That's the word she used. And the verse says she had compassion on him. I think a crying baby got to her before anything else did.

Egyptian is a fair guess, friend. She's Pharaoh's daughter, standing at the Nile, so you'd expect that word. But she opens the basket and says, “This is one of the Hebrew children.” (Exodus 2:6) That's what she called him. And the verse says she had compassion on him.

Desert, baker? I can see why you'd go there. Moses does spend time in dry country later, but that's not this scene. She names him Moses and explains, “I drew him out of the water.” (Exodus 2:10) This baby was in a basket along the Nile. The story isn't over, though.

Mountains, friend? That's aiming high, I'll give you that. But this boy was in a basket among the reeds along the Nile, not on a peak. (Exodus 2:3) She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.” (Exodus 2:10) The name comes from that moment at the river.

problems.problem: The text says she identified him as a Hebrew child, not that she knew exactly who he was. It also does not say the whole palace was running on one rule or that she was holding him.
Saying she had compassion on him 'anyway' implies that his being a Hebrew child was a reason she might not have had compassion. The text does not say that.
The claim that much of Moses's story happens in dry country refers to events outside this passage without a reference.
The passage does not say there was no sand in the scene.
The passage does not mention a splash.
Saying 'even I know water when I see it' talks down to the baker for choosing the answer.
